newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Reserve Bank seen behind rise in S.African shortage.
newsitem.headline: Reserve Bank seen behind rise in S.African shortage.

text.p: South Africa's money market shortage rose to 9.258 billion rand on Monday from 8.238 billion rand on Saturday after the Reserve Bank drained liquidity after what dealers said on Tuesday were overdone falls last week.
The dealers however said they saw the market shortage drifting lower to around seven billion rand later in the month on the back of strong bond and currency markets.
"I think things were a little bit overdone last week. The Reserve Bank said they were happy with a shortage of nine billion. The money market gets away from itself too quickly," one dealer said.
"The Reserve Bank is wanting a more gradual easing of money market conditions. It's not a bad thing where it (the shortage) is," he added.
Last month, Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said a high money market shortage helped the authorities keep a rein on bank credit extension and he was in no hurry to see it lower.
"There are some advantages from a monetary policy point of view in having a money market shortage that is staying relatively high all the time," Stals told Reuters.
"It gives us a much greater influence on bank credit extension and the money supply. We are in no hurry to try and reduce the shortage," he said.

Another dealer commented: "The shortage is artificially held up because the Reserve Bank is trying to keep short interest rates higher. But we should see liquidity coming back into the market because bonds are very, very strong."
The South African bond market maintained its bull run early on Tuesday on continued good foreign demand and positive sentiment about economic fundamentals.
